decisions.reason: As a bread close to the core range that was still shown after launch, it likely has become part of normal bakery operations, and even without strong public commitment management has some incentive to continue rather than admit the launch was unnecessary.

This sweet pastry fits the firm's established confectionery business well, so disappointing results can easily be treated as temporary while management prefers to retain a low-risk extension of the core offer.

The farmhouse bread is close to the core assortment but is newer and less visibly committed than the others, so it has a somewhat higher exit risk, though management would still tend to persist with a familiar bread-line launch.

Because the poppy seed Christmas stollen was presented as a flagship and highlighted on its own page with a gold award, management is strongly committed publicly and is very unlikely to withdraw it soon.

The premium Christmas stollen also carries a visible gold-award claim and sits squarely in the firm's seasonal specialty tradition, giving management clear reasons to continue it rather than reverse course.
